name: Make bread from scratch
blurb: A basic yeasted loaf teaches the whole grammar of bread: hydration, gluten development, fermentation and the shaping that gives structure. It is a fortnight to a genuinely good loaf.
gear: Strong bread flour, salt, instant yeast
A digital scale — volume measures are unreliable
A Dutch oven or a baking stone
steps: Weigh everything and work in baker’s percentages: flour 100%, water 65–75%, salt 2%, yeast 1%.
Mix and rest for 30 minutes before kneading — the autolyse does much of the gluten work for you.
Knead or do a set of stretch-and-folds until the dough passes the windowpane test.
Bulk ferment until roughly doubled, judging by the dough rather than the clock — temperature changes everything.
Shape with tension across the surface, then prove until a poked indent springs back slowly.
Bake hot with steam for the first ten minutes, then dry, and cool completely on a rack before cutting.
tips: Under-proving gives a dense crumb; over-proving gives a flat, collapsing loaf. Learn the poke test.
Cutting a hot loaf gives a gummy crumb. Wait an hour, however hard that is.
Weigh, do not scoop. Cup measures of flour vary by 30%.
proof: A loaf with an open crumb, crisp crust and good oven spring, repeated three times.
